findings.what: The icon is tiny, about 40px, and a stray white pip overlaps it. The weapon stat line starts with 'dmg' clipped by that pip ('dmg' reads as 'dnig'). The stats are two lines of tightly packed text in one colour with no hierarchy. '12 / 24' at the right has no label. 'integrity 100/100' is mixed in with 'armour 0 backpack 4 belt 1', which are unrelated figures.
findings.fix: Put the weapon in a --ui-raised panel with a 64px icon, 16px padding and a 3px rarity bar. Move the pip away from the text. Lay the stats out in a 4-column grid with 24px gutters: label 16px tx-2 above value 20px tx-1. Label '12 / 24' as ammo, or remove it.

findings.where: Hierarchy (title y 362, 'armour plate' y 792, 'scav pistol' y 448)
findings.what: The title 'backpack', 'armour plate' and 'scav pistol' are all bold condensed type in similar weights. The eye lands on the title and 'armour plate' with nothing separating them. The slot grid, which is the main content, has the least contrast on the card. The lime selected-slot frame is the only accent and it is small.
findings.fix: Make the title 32px f-cond 700 and both item names 20px f-cond 600 tx-1. Let the lime selected frame and the 'use' button be the only accents on the card.

findings.what: 'equipped' is a bare grey label with no divider above or panel behind it. The vertical gaps (413 to 448 to 484 to 515 to 548) are uneven, and the hairline dividers at y 535 and y 782 are almost invisible. The result is a stack of text lines, not sections.
findings.fix: Set labels at 16px tx-2 weight 600 with +.04em tracking. Use 24px gaps between sections and 1px --ui-line dividers.

findings.where: Surrounding HUD (top-right panels, left log chips)
findings.what: The run info panel and the left log chips use different panel fills and borders from the backpack card, and the lime-bordered slot, amber contract chip and teal extraction chip all compete near the card. This is the HUD corner the owner has set aside, so only a note, not a fix, applies to this screen.
findings.fix: Dim the HUD with the --scrim behind the card so the card is the only bright layer.

v.verdict: The only change is a small x button in the corner, and it sits beside the old 'b or i to close' text. The rest of the card still looks like a debug panel: the slots are bare, the item detail is flat, and the stats are one cramped line.

findings.where: close x (1345-1383 x 327-363) and 'b or i to close' text (y 367)
findings.what: The close is now shown twice, once as an x and once as a text hint. The x is a small outlined square pushed into the corner. It overlaps the top edge of the header row, and the hint text sits only 18px to its left, below it.
findings.fix: Delete the 'b or i to close' text. Make the x a 32px button, 16px from the card's top and right edges, with a 'b' key-cap chip beside it. Align its centre with the title baseline at y 362.

findings.where: selected item block (y 780-880), 'use' / 'armor' row and hint line
findings.what: The 'use' and 'armor' pair is a bare label with no button. The hint line 'arrows move  z drop one  drag to tactical belt' is plain 16px text that explains instead of showing keys. 'armor' conflicts with 'armour' elsewhere on the card. The block has no panel, so it floats on the card.
findings.fix: Put the block in a --ui-raised pane with 16px padding. Make 'use' a lime --acc button with --acc-ink text and an 'e' key-cap chip. Change 'armor' to 'armour'. Render the hints as key-cap chips (1px --ui-line-hi border, 8px gaps) in a footer row. Cut 'drag to tactical belt'.

findings.what: The 16 slots are dark squares with only a subtle outline. They have no rarity bars, and the selected slot is the only one with a clear frame. The grid has no count, so the player can't tell how full the bag is. The item counts ('2') and pips sit on the icons with no contrast backing.
findings.fix: Give each slot a --ui-bg fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, a 4px radius and an 8px gap. Add a 3px rarity bar along the bottom of each filled slot. Show '3 / 16' at 16px tx-2 in the section header. Put the item count in a small --ui-void chip.

findings.what: The weapon icon is tiny (about 40px) and its pip overlaps the 'dmg' text. The stats are two run-on lines ('dmg 23 range 42m semi mag 12 / integrity 100/100 armour 0 backpack 4 belt 1') with no structure. The '12 / 24' on the right has no label. The card has no divider between the equipped block and the grid.
findings.fix: Put the weapon in a --ui-raised panel with a 64px icon, 16px padding and a 3px rarity bar. Move the pip clear of the text. Lay the stats out in a 4-column grid with 24px gutters: label 16px tx-2 above value 20px tx-1. Label '12 / 24' as 'ammo'.

findings.where: card frame (530-1390 x 318-921) and hotbar overlap (y 921-950)
findings.what: The card is about 45% of the screen wide and nearly touches the hotbar, leaving 29px. The backdrop is not dimmed, so the busy map competes with the card edges. The guide says windows should fill about 90% of the screen.
findings.fix: Put --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) behind the card. Either grow the card to about 90% of the screen, or lift it so there is at least 24px between its bottom edge and the hotbar tooltip.

findings.what: The title, 'armour plate' and 'scav pistol' all read as bold white condensed text at similar sizes, so the eye has no clear first stop. The selected item name is nearly as large as the title. The text colours are all near-white, with no tx-2 separation.
findings.fix: Make the title 32px f-cond 700. Make both item names 20px f-cond 600 tx-1. Make labels ('equipped', 'use', stats) 16px tx-2. Let the lime selected frame and the 'use' button be the only accents on the card.

findings.what: The space between the grid and the selected item (about 45px) is dead, and the card bottom (y 880-921) is empty. Spacing between sections is uneven: 24px at the top, then 45px.
findings.fix: Use a consistent 24px between sections. Add a 1px --ui-line divider above the selected item pane. Trim the bottom padding to 24px.

findings.where: small text across the card (labels at about 14px)
findings.what: 'equipped', the stats and the hint line look about 14-15px with a text shadow. They are hard to read from a couch at 1080. The pixel-looking render of the condensed type has jagged edges.
findings.fix: Set every read-only label to at least 16px with +.04em tracking in tx-2 #aaa498. Keep 14px only for the version stamp and legal text.

v.verdict: The controls panel is much better: it has key caps, grouped sections and a tidy two-column layout. The raid HUD around it is still crowded, with the run-info card, the left log and the panel's position all unresolved.

findings.what: This is still the densest block on screen. It has six rows of 20px-ish text with no group spacing, the 'dawn clear' line is a stray, and the caret is tiny. The header and body weights are nearly equal. Text spans nearly the full card width and the counts are not aligned in a column. My earlier advice on this card was not followed.
findings.fix: Drop 'dawn clear'. Set the 'contracts' and 'run goals' headers to 16px f-cond 600 tx-2 with 16px space above. Set the rows to 20px tx-1. Right-align the counts in a column at x 1880. Widen the card to 360px.

findings.what: The panel is better but still floats at x 493. It has no tie to the 24px margin or to the hotbar and the 'standing' chip, so it sits in the middle of the playfield. It is about 265px wide with 22px row pitch, and its top edge at y 608 is higher than any other left element. The 'move' action word is also repeated, as both a section title and a row.
findings.fix: Anchor the panel's left edge at x 24 and its bottom edge 16px above the 'standing' chip (about y 930). Make the row pitch 24px. Rename the 'move' section header to 'movement', or merge it so it is not a duplicate of the 'move' row.

findings.where: controls panel text, section labels and action words
findings.what: The section labels 'move', 'fight', 'gear' and 'raid' are about 12-13px in dim grey, below the 16px floor. The action words (move, sprint, next gun) are also about 14px. Key caps are drawn smaller than the words beside them, so the keys, which should lead, look weaker than the labels.
findings.fix: Set labels to 16px f-cond 600 tx-2 with +.04em tracking. Set key caps to 16px tx-1 on --ui-raised with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Set action words to 16px tx-1 or tx-2. Raise the panel padding to 16px.

findings.what: The log stack runs directly into the controls panel's left edge (x 493) and shares the y band 700-800. Its rows are different widths with a left bar, and the rows look like four unrelated chips. 'running slowly' is a new, dimmer row that does not match the others.
findings.fix: Move the whole log up above the panel and cap it at 3 rows. Give every row the same 16px label size, one left bar colour and one fill. Make 'running slowly' match the others or drop it.

findings.what: The 'golden enemy' and 'stronghold' chips are stacked and pile onto the red bots at x 1090-1170, so they overlap the world art. They are also different widths with a ragged left edge. The order flipped from the old version for no reason.
findings.fix: Centre both chips under the 'extract 152m' tag at a fixed width of 300px with 8px between them. Keep the order stable between versions.

findings.where: collapse carets, x 345-358 y 154, x 1880-1895 y 103
findings.what: Two carets remain, on the bots list and run info. The controls panel dropped its caret, so the three cards no longer share one behaviour. Each caret is about 12px, too small to hit with a pad, and it has no focus state.
findings.fix: Use one pattern across all three cards. Make it a 16px chevron with a pad-visible focus ring, or remove carets and use a single key hint such as 'f2 hide' in the 16px footer.

findings.where: controls panel footer, 'f1 full list' x 503-577, y 842-860
findings.what: The footer hint is dim 14px grey and sits tight under the 'x extract' row (22px gap). It reads as an extra row, not a footer. In career mode the owner wanted the list folded and F1 to open it, and the hint does not say that F1 also closes it.
findings.fix: Add a 1px --ui-line divider and 8px space above the footer. Set the hint to 16px tx-2 as 'f1 hide' or 'f1 full list', right-aligned.

findings.what: The panel looks like a near-black translucent fill with a dark edge and no 1px --ui-line-hi border. It is the same flat black box as the other cards but with no distinguishing edge or accent, so it reads as a template box on the busy tiles.
findings.fix: Use an opaque --ui-panel fill (#16191b) with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a 4px radius, the same as the bots list and run info cards.

v.verdict: The raid HUD has a strong ammo block and hotbar, but the top-right money strip overprints itself, the controls list sits in the middle of play, and sizes and panel styles drift from one corner to the next.

findings.what: The text overprints: '$900' collides with '$90' and a second '$0', and 'stash $0 bag $0' runs off the right edge. The money is unreadable and the strip looks broken. It also shows stash and backpack twice, in two different type sizes.
findings.fix: Rebuild it as one vertical 1x1 list (cw-trcol), with each item 20px f-cond, label 16px tx-2 on the left and value tx-1 right-aligned. Use one font size, keep a 16px inset, and don't draw each value twice. Contain it in a panel with 8px padding.

findings.what: The full-height controls panel with about 22 key rows sits in the middle of the playfield, next to the player and the extraction ring. It is clutter and covers the action. The ruling says it should be folded to one short line at mid-bottom left, and F1 should open it.
findings.fix: Collapse it to a single 16px line ('f1 controls') anchored at x=5% from the left, bottom 120px. Open the full list only on F1. Never show it open by default in a career raid.

findings.where: HUD panels overall (kill list, minimap, run info, controls, ammo)
findings.what: The panels don't share a style. They differ in fill opacity, border, corner radius and padding. The minimap is near-black, the kill list is translucent, and the ammo card is solid. Header sizes also differ ('current pillager bots 0' at about 16px bold, 'run info' at about 18px). Collapse chevrons appear on some panels and not others.
findings.fix: Use one panel recipe: --ui-panel at 88% alpha, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 16px padding, header 16px f-cond 600 tx-2. Put the chevron on every collapsible panel in the same place.

findings.what: There are 7 rows of 'dead', each with a dash, in muted grey at about 14px. This repeats the same information and lowers the contrast. The lines are cramped, with a 17px pitch. The pink 'fbi_surveillance_van' adds a stray colour that isn't a defined player colour.
findings.fix: Show only the live count and the 'you' line, or fold the dead rows into 'x out · 7 dead'. If the rows stay, use a 16px minimum, tx-2 text at 4.5:1 and a 24px row pitch. Drop the off-palette pink, or use --acc only if it means selected.

findings.what: The hp bar is a saturated green with a big '100' that has no clear hierarchy against the ammo block. The 'stamina' label is crowded on the bar. The 'standing' pill is a third, different panel style. The bars run only to x430 and don't align with the hotbar edge at y955.
findings.fix: Make hp and stamina the same height (24px) with the label 16px and the value right-aligned inside. Keep hp as the single bold element (56px hero only for ammo). Align the baselines of the bars with the hotbar slot bottoms, and restyle 'standing' as a quiet 16px tx-2 tag.

findings.where: top-centre timer and extract chip, and 'extraction a available' tag
findings.what: '9:00' is good as a hero number, but the chip below it ('extract 38m') is teal on dark teal with thin contrast. The left tag reads 'extraction a available', a typo or stray letter. Both teal chips use different padding and radius from the other panels.
findings.fix: Fix the string to 'extraction available'. Use --extract text on --ui-panel with 8px 16px padding and 4px radius, and use the same chip style for both.

findings.what: The hotbar is neat, but 6 of the 9 slots are dim silhouettes at low contrast, so they look disabled. The selected slot 2 has a yellow border and slot 4 has a blue one, so two states compete. The tiny ammo counts ('60') are about 12px.
findings.fix: Give empty slots a flat --ui-raised fill with a 1px --ui-line border and no silhouette. Use the lime border only for the selected slot, and give the 'f' slot a quiet label tag. Make ammo numbers 16px minimum.

findings.what: The body text is about 18px in four mixed colours (white, green, and tx-2), with objective lines like 'no heals yet' and 'no elite killed yet' in green. Green means 'ok', so it reads as completed when it isn't. A faint crosshair watermark sits at the right edge, and the corner has a hatch mark.
findings.fix: Keep unfinished objectives in tx-1 with progress counts in tx-2, and use --ok green only on completed ones. Remove the watermark and the hatch. Use a 20px row pitch of 28px.

v.verdict: The raid HUD has a readable ammo hero and a clear weapon bar, but the top-right money strip prints overlapping text, the controls card sits open in mid-screen, and the five corner panels use different type sizes, borders and fills.

findings.where: top-right money strip (cash / xp / stash / bag)
findings.what: Text collides: '$900' prints twice over itself ('$900$90 0'), and 'stash $0 bag $0' overlaps 'xp' and runs against the panel edge. It is a render bug, unreadable, and it sits in the most-read corner. It also clashes with the 'stash $0 / backpack $0' row below it, so the same values appear twice.
findings.fix: Draw each value once in a 2-column list: label at 16px tx-2, value at 20px tx-1 right-aligned, 8px row gap, 16px padding. Drop the duplicated stash and bag entries. Follow the cw-trcol vertical list.

findings.what: The full controls list is open over the playfield, covering the route and the extraction ring area. This contradicts the owner's ruling that in a career raid the list sits mid-bottom left and starts folded to one line. It also adds 20+ rows of clutter that compete with the weapon bar.
findings.fix: Fold it to a single 'f1 controls' line at 16px at x≈5%, y≈1040 and open it on F1. Keep it open only in the party demo.

findings.where: all HUD panels (pillager list, money, minimap, run info, controls, ammo)
findings.what: They don't match. Fills run from black to translucent grey, corner radii and borders vary, and the type mixes about 14, 15, 17, 18 and 22px with different weights. The pillager list and run info show no clear title hierarchy, and 'run info' uses the same weight as its contract lines. This reads as six different widgets rather than one system.
findings.fix: One panel: fill #16191b at 90%, 1px #4a5257 border, 4px radius, 16px padding. Title 16px f-cond 600 tx-2; body 20px tx-1 (labels 16px tx-2). Same collapse chevron on every panel.

findings.what: The stamina and hp bars use different fills (blue, green) and heavy label text. The 'hp 100' label is oversized and bold, so it fights the 56px ammo hero for attention. 'standing' is a boxed pill that nothing else uses. The stamina label is low-contrast white on light blue.
findings.fix: Make both bars 12px tall with a #1e2225 track. Put the hp number at 32px, but only 800 weight for the one hero. Set the labels at 16px tx-1 above the bars. Show the posture as plain 16px tx-2 text with no pill.

findings.what: Selection is split: slot 2 has a lime frame and slot 4 has a blue tint with an 'f' badge, so it is unclear which gun is active. Empty slots 3 and 5-0 are drawn as faint silhouettes and cost the bar a lot of space for no information. The 'compact smg  fire use' tab above it is cramped, and it mixes two weights.
findings.fix: Use only lime for the active slot (3px border) and a 1px line border for the others. Dim the empty slots to 40% and shrink them to icon-only cells. Drop the blue tint and put 'f' in the label. Align the hint line to the bar's left edge at 16px.

findings.where: top centre (9:00, extract 38m) and 'extraction a available'
findings.what: The timer is white, thin and bold-ish, with no panel, over a busy map, so its contrast changes with the terrain. 'extraction a available' reads like a typo, uses a different teal pill from 'extract 38m', and is far from the other one.
findings.fix: Put the 9:00 timer at 32px f-cond 800 on a --scrim pill. Fix the string ('extraction available'). Use one --extract chip style for both labels, 16px, 8px padding.

findings.what: The map is large (about 300x300) and mostly empty black, with small white strips and tiny player markers that are hard to read. The clipped glyph 'n' by the markers and the circle 'a' look like debug marks.
findings.fix: Shrink it to about 220px, add a 1px line border and make the markers 12px. Remove the stray labels or place them as 16px compass letters outside the frame.

findings.what: The '30 / 60' hero is strong, but the card text 'b / i backpack' and '3 items $1,370' is 14px and low contrast. It also repeats the $1,370 on the pillager list. A third lime-free card style joins the others.
findings.fix: Raise the footer lines to 16px tx-2 and keep one value location. Use the shared panel style.

v.verdict: This is a clean, readable column menu with a clear lime primary action. The orange gradient logo, the tiny low-contrast secondary text and the cramped saves block keep it from looking polished.

findings.what: The orange-gold gradient wordmark with a drop shadow is the loudest thing on screen. It uses a heavy display face and a gradient wash, which the guide bans. It also sits next to the lime button as two competing hot colours, and gold sits 24 degrees of hue from lime. Boldness should go in one place only.
findings.fix: Set the title in Barlow Condensed 700 at 32px or the 56px hero size, solid --tx-1 with no gradient or shadow. Leave lime to the primary button. If a logo is wanted, make it art that uses neither gold nor lime.

findings.where: Secondary buttons (2 player co-op, 2 player arcade demo, 1 player arcade demo)
findings.what: The three outlined buttons are the same weight and size as each other. Two of them are demo variants that sit in the main play column at equal rank. Their idle borders are very faint. The menu has no tier between the main play modes and the demo modes.
findings.fix: Keep '1 player' and '2 player co-op' as the main two. Move the two demos to a smaller text-link row or into a section below, at 16px in --tx-2. Use a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a --ui-panel fill on the rest.

findings.where: Saves block (label, save row, name input and its two buttons)
findings.what: The 'saves' label is about 14px in dim grey and fails the 4.5:1 floor. The selected save row uses lime text on a dark fill, and lime text should be reserved for focus. The name input and the 'change name' and 'create a new save' buttons are tiny, 16px or smaller, and crowded under the list. The input has no label and no visible difference from the buttons beside it.
findings.fix: Make the 'saves' label 16px --tx-2 with +.04em tracking, and put a 24px gap above it. Show the selected save with a lime 3px left bar and a --ui-raised fill, with the name in --tx-1. Use 20px row text, and put 16px between the list and the name controls. Label the input 'name' or give it placeholder text, and use 40px button heights.

findings.what: The legend has 14px text in dim grey. The key caps are tiny and have a white fill that is brighter than the text. The legend shows move, aim, fire, search and controls on the main menu, which is clutter and not actionable here. The version stamp is tiny, at the far left, and does not line up with the legend or the top-right buttons.
findings.fix: Drop the legend from this screen, or show only 'f1 controls'. Make the key caps 16px with a --ui-line-hi outline and a --ui-raised fill. Align the version to the 5% margin on the same baseline as the legend.

findings.what: The two buttons are small, at about 14px text, with thin borders, and they are close to the corner. They do not share the column's button style. The text is bold white on near-black with little padding, and the focus state is not visible.
findings.fix: Use the same 4px-radius outline button as the column, 16px f-cond 600 text, 40px height, 24px padding, and place them on the 5% margin (96px). Give pad focus a lime 2px outline.

findings.what: The tagline is about 18px in mid grey with a pixel-shadow look. It has low contrast against the busy background and sits tight under the title at about 30px to the button.
findings.fix: Set it at 20px in --tx-2 (#aaa498) with +.04em tracking, and make the gap 24px above the first button.

findings.what: The map is dimmed, but its coloured pools and large grey and blue rectangles still show behind the column. They read as visual noise, and the column has no panel to separate it from them.
findings.fix: Put the column on a --ui-panel card at 90% opacity with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Alternatively, raise the scrim to rgba(6,7,8,.80) and add a blur.

findings.what: The fill is a good lime, but the label text is only 20px and sits tight in a 56px button. The button width is slightly different from the saves block, and there is no focus ring other than the fill.
findings.fix: Use 24px f-cond 700 text in --acc-ink with +.04em tracking. Match the width exactly to the column (558px) and add a 2px --acc-hover outline on pad focus.

v.verdict: A clean, centred title menu with a clear lime primary action, but the orange gradient logo breaks the one-accent palette, the type is small for a couch, and the lower half is cluttered with too many same-weight controls.

findings.what: The wordmark is an orange-to-amber gradient with a drop shadow. That is a second hot colour next to the lime accent, and the guide bans gradients and says to keep gold and lime apart. Both the logo and the lime '1 player' bar compete for first look, so boldness is in two places.
findings.fix: Make the wordmark flat --tx-1 (#efe9dc) at f-cond 800, 56px hero size, with no gradient or shadow. Or make it the only lime element and give '1 player' a quieter focus bar.

findings.where: Menu button stack (1 player, 2 player co-op, arcade demos)
findings.what: Four full-width buttons of equal weight sit in one column. Two of them are demos, which are secondary, yet they get the same size and priority as co-op. The labels are 20px or less, small for a 1080 couch view, and the tight 8px gaps read as a block.
findings.fix: Keep '1 player' and '2 player co-op' as primary rows at 20px/600 and 56px tall. Move both demos into a smaller 16px secondary row or a 'demos' group with a 24px gap above. Match the row heights; they currently look like 56 vs 48.

findings.where: Saves block (saves label, pillager new row, name field + 2 buttons)
findings.what: The 'saves' label is dim grey at about 14px, below the 16px minimum and the 4.5:1 floor. The save row is outlined in lime, so it looks like a second selected item next to the filled '1 player'. The name input and its two buttons form a cramped, unequal strip.
findings.fix: Set the 'saves' label to 16px --tx-2 (#aaa498) with +.04em tracking. Make the save row's idle border --ui-line-hi and use lime only on actual focus. Give the input and buttons one 48px height and 16px gaps, and move the strip 24px below the save row.

findings.where: Footer key hints (wasd move, mouse aim, lmb fire, e search, f1 controls)
findings.what: The hints are about 14-15px and dim, and the key caps are tiny and bold. They sit far from everything else at the bottom centre. A title menu doesn't need a raid controls legend, so it is clutter. The version stamp 'v0.1148' is also tiny and very low contrast.
findings.fix: Cut the legend to nav hints only (select, back), at 16px --tx-2. Move the raid controls to the controls screen. Set the version to 14px at --tx-2, aligned to the 5% margin.

findings.what: Both are small 16px-ish outlined chips on a busy background. They differ in width and have heavy bold labels. 'go fullscreen' is a system utility but gets the same weight as 'settings'.
findings.fix: Make both 48px tall with equal 16px padding. Set the label weight to 600. Turn 'go fullscreen' into an icon button. Align them to the 5% margin (96px right, 54px top).

findings.what: The tagline is about 18px grey with a heavy letter-spacing look, sitting close under a big logo. The periods have a faux-stylised look. It is low contrast on the dark scrim and the gap to the buttons is only about 24px.
findings.fix: Use 20px --tx-2 f-cond 600. Leave 16px under the logo and 32px above the first button.

findings.what: The blurred scene is busy, with bright blue and green rectangles and tinted circles, at 80% dim. It adds mottled noise behind the text, and the bright vertical bars at the left and right pull the eye away from the menu.
findings.fix: Raise the scrim to --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) plus a radial vignette. Drop the blur on the bright blocks, or lower scene saturation by about 40%.

findings.what: The menu column is 558px wide and centred, but the saves row and input strip use a different inner rhythm to the buttons above, and the 4px radius is consistent only in part. The spacing between groups (8, 8, 8, 28, 12) is off the 8px grid.
findings.fix: Use 8px gaps within a group and 24px between groups. Hold a 4px radius on all controls. Snap all heights to 48/56.

v.verdict: The title screen is clean and the lime 1 player button is the clear first read. Almost none of the earlier advice was applied: the gold gradient wordmark, four equal-weight buttons, the weak saves block, the legend and the top-right buttons are all as before.

findings.what: The wordmark is still a gold-to-orange gradient with a drop shadow. That is the gradient wash the guide bans. It sits close to the lime accent in hue and competes with the 1 player button. It is also the only element in a heavy display weight.
findings.fix: Use Barlow Condensed 700 or 800 at 56px (hero), solid --tx-1 (#efe9dc), no gradient and no shadow. Or use real logo art that avoids both gold and lime. Keep a 24px gap to the tagline.

findings.where: buttons 2 player co-op, 2 player arcade demo, 1 player arcade demo
findings.what: Three outlined buttons of the same width and height make a monotone stack. The two demos have the same weight as co-op, which buries the real choices. The co-op label also carries a parenthetical, '(same machine)'. The column is 558px wide, which is too wide for a calm column menu.
findings.fix: Keep 1 player (lime) and 2 player co-op as the two main buttons, with 20px text and 48px height. Move the two demos to a 16px --tx-2 text-link row below them, or into a 'demos' group. Drop '(same machine)' or move it to a 16px --tx-2 sub-label. Narrow the column to about 440px.

findings.where: saves block (label, row, name input, change name, create a new save)
findings.what: The 'saves' label is small, dim and has only 16px of space above it. The selected save has only a thin lime outline and lime text. The input and its buttons are cramped at 38px tall, and the input has no label. Lime text on the save name is also used outside the primary action. The three controls are different widths with uneven gaps.
findings.fix: Set the 'saves' label at 16px --tx-2 with +.04em tracking and 24px above it. Selected row: --ui-raised fill, 3px lime left bar, name in --tx-1 at 20px, no full lime outline. Leave 16px between the list and the controls. Make the controls 40px high with equal 8px gaps. Add a 'name' label or placeholder. Make 'create a new save' the quieter text-style action.

findings.what: The buttons are 46px tall with 16px padding and sit at about 96px from the right and 33px from the top. They are not on the 5% margin. They are heavier than they need to be, and their text is tiny and bold.
findings.fix: Put both on the 5% margin (96px from the top and right). Use the 4px-radius outline button with 16px f-cond 600 text, 40px height and 24px padding. Give pad focus a 2px lime outline.

findings.what: The legend is a full control list on the title screen, which is clutter. The key caps are tiny, with white fill and dark text, and look unlike the other buttons. The version stamp sits at about 96px from the left, but on a different baseline from the legend. The text is under 14px and dim.
findings.fix: Cut the legend to 'f1 controls', or remove it. Key caps: 16px, --ui-raised fill, 1px --ui-line-hi outline, --tx-1 text. Put v0.1148 at 14px on the same baseline as the legend, at the 96px margin.

findings.what: The '32 fps | screen 60' badge is lime on black with a lime border. It looks like a debug overlay. It also uses the accent for something that is not a focus or selection.
findings.fix: Hide it outside debug mode. If it stays, use 14px --tx-2 text, no border and no fill, on the 5% margin.

findings.what: The tagline is dim grey on a dark scene at about 18px, and its contrast is marginal. It also sits close to the title, with a 24px gap to the first button.
findings.fix: Use --tx-2 (#aaa498) at 20px with +.04em tracking. Keep 16px between title and tagline and 32px between tagline and the button column.

findings.what: The blurred, darkened game scene has flat translucent rectangles and glow ellipses that read as placeholder shapes. The scene has no focal point, and the left and right are symmetrical clutter behind a centred column.
findings.fix: Add a --scrim at .80 plus a vignette so the scene stays dim. Or replace it with one lit hero shot placed off-centre.

v.verdict: The calm column with one lime primary row is solid and readable, but the amber-gradient wordmark, equal-weight demo rows, mixed lime in the save strip and the key-hint legend still make it look assembled rather than designed.

findings.what: The orange-amber gradient with drop shadow was not changed. It brings in a second hot colour, sits about 24 degrees of hue from the lime button, and is the template-gradient look the guide bans. The result is two competing hero elements, wordmark and lime button, and the lime row below it feels cheap by comparison.
findings.fix: Make the wordmark flat --tx-1 #efe9dc at f-cond 800, 56px or larger, with no gradient and no shadow, and leave lime only on the focused row. Or keep it big (about 96px) and flat. Delete the amber fill.

findings.where: menu stack: 2 player arcade demo and 1 player arcade demo
findings.what: The two demos use the same 48px row, border and 20px weight as the real co-op mode, so five modes read as equals. 1 player is a 56px lime slab and 2 player co-op is the only other real mode, but the demos are the same size as it. The gaps are also uneven (about 8px between rows, then a jump to saves).
findings.fix: Keep 1 player and 2 player co-op as 56px primary rows. Make both demos 40px, 16px, --tx-2 text, with no border or a --ui-line border, and put them 24px below co-op. Use a constant 8px gap inside a group.

findings.what: There are two lime elements in one column: the filled 1 player and the lime outlined save row with lime text 'pillager new'. Lime is meant to mean 'selected' once, so the save row looks like a second focus. The 'saves' label is small and dim, around 14px, and below the 4.5:1 target. The input and its buttons are 38px tall, which does not match the 56 or 48 rows above, and the row gets tight spacing under the save row.
findings.fix: Set the 'saves' label to 16px --tx-2 with +.04em tracking. Give the save row a --ui-line-hi border and --tx-1 name text, with lime only on actual focus. Make the input and both buttons 48px tall with 16px gaps. Put the strip 24px below the save row and align it to the stack's 558px width.

findings.where: footer key hints (wasd move, mouse aim, lmb fire, e search, f1 controls)
findings.what: The legend is five items of raid instructions on the title screen, which is clutter. Its labels are about 15px muted grey, low contrast on the dark scene. The version 'v0.1148' is tiny, at 12px or smaller and bold, and sits at x=96 while the legend is centred, so they do not share a baseline or margin.
findings.fix: Cut the legend to nav hints only (select, back) at 16px --tx-2, or move the raid keys to the controls screen. Set the version to 14px f-body 500 in --tx-2, aligned to the 5% margin (96px left, 54px from the bottom) on the same baseline as the hints.

findings.where: top-right go fullscreen and settings buttons
findings.what: Both buttons are 48px tall, but their labels are small bold text of about 15px. The pair floats at x≈1823 rather than the 5% margin (96px), and 'go fullscreen' is a long text label for a utility. Neither lines up with the 558px menu column or the fps badge at top-left.
findings.fix: Turn 'go fullscreen' into a 48px square icon button. Set labels to 16px/600, and put the pair at right 96px, top 54px with a 16px gap. Move the fps badge to the same 96px / 54px margin or hide it outside debug.

findings.what: The tagline is a dim 18px line in grey that is close to the background. It is decoration, not hierarchy, and it floats 40px below the wordmark, about 35px above the first button, which is neither grouped with the title nor the menu.
findings.fix: Set it to 16px --tx-2 with +.04em tracking, 16px below the wordmark and 32px above 1 player. Or delete it for less clutter.

findings.what: The background is a dimmed, blurred raid map with floating pastel rectangles and ellipses that look like debug art, with no focal point or vignette tied to the menu. It makes the identity weak and adds noise behind the label text, and the scene shows no character or key art.
findings.fix: Raise the scrim to rgba(6,7,8,.80) over the whole scene and add a radial vignette. Better, replace it with one hero key-art silhouette (a mech or a pillager) on the left third so the menu column has a real counterweight.

v.verdict: The busy sprite backdrop is gone and the menu now reads clearly on a calm dark vignette, but the gold gradient logo, the four same-weight mode rows and the cramped saves block are all still unchanged and generic.

findings.what: The logo is still an orange-gold gradient wordmark with a drop shadow. It competes with the lime '1 player' bar, so two things shout. Gold is meant for rarity only, and a gradient is a template tell.
findings.fix: Make the wordmark flat. Use tx-1 #efe9dc at 56px f-cond 800 with no gradient and no shadow, or use flat --acc. Remove the shadow.

findings.what: The 1 player bar is a good hero. The other three rows are identical 48px outlined boxes, so '2 player arcade demo' and '1 player arcade demo' look as important as co-op. 'Same machine' in brackets is explaining text.
findings.fix: Keep co-op as the only secondary row. Put the two arcade demos in a single 16px tx-2 row of two small buttons with a 16px gap, or move them into a submenu. Drop '(same machine)' or make it a 16px tx-2 sub-label.

findings.what: The sprite background was removed and replaced with a near-black vignette. This is calm but the screen now has no identity. A 560px column floats in a 1920x1080 void with 300px empty above the logo and 270px below the saves. It could be any app.
findings.fix: Add one controlled art element. For example, a darkened key-art plate at 30 percent opacity behind the column, or a left-aligned layout with the menu in a 560px column at x 96 and hero art on the right. At the least, add a hairline --ui-line panel (--ui-panel, 4px radius, 24px padding) behind the column.

findings.what: The 'saves' label is small and dim, about 14px grey. The pillager new row is a thin lime outline with lime text, which makes lime a label colour. The name field, 'change name' and 'create a new save' are three different fills and widths. The gap from the mode list (28px) is barely more than the gap between the mode rows (8px).
findings.fix: Make the label 16px tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better. Use a --ui-raised fill with a 3px lime left bar for the selected save, and tx-1 for the name. Give the three bottom controls one fill, --ui-panel with a --ui-line-hi border. Put 32px between the mode list and the saves.

findings.what: The tagline is about 18px grey and tightly set between the logo and the first button, with about 20px above it. It reads as an afterthought and is a slogan, not information.
findings.fix: Set it at 20px --tx-2 with +.04em tracking, with 16px between the logo and the tagline and 40px between the tagline and the buttons. Or delete it.

findings.where: bottom key legend (y 1030-1055) and version stamp
findings.what: The legend keycaps are about 14px and the version stamp is dim 14px at x 96, so the baselines and left margins do not match the 5 percent margin used by the top-right buttons (x 1611-1823). The legend sits very close to the bottom edge. The control hints are also shown on the title screen where they do nothing.
findings.fix: Set the legend and version stamp to a shared baseline at y 1020, with a 96px left and right margin. Set the legend labels to 16px tx-2. Keep the keycaps with a --ui-line-hi border.

findings.what: They are small 14-16px labels in boxes with a heavy white border, which makes them brighter than the saves controls and the second-tier mode rows. They are the brightest outlines on screen after the hero.
findings.fix: Use a --ui-line-hi border, 16px label in tx-2, a 48px height to match the mode rows, and 16px between them. Move the border to tx-1 only on focus.

v.verdict: This is a readable raid HUD with a strong ammo hero number, but it has too many competing small panels, a duplicated extraction message, and mixed panel styles and colours, so it looks assembled rather than designed.

findings.where: top-centre banner stack (8:59 / extract 152m / extraction c available)
findings.what: Two teal pills say the same thing, and a stray cyan arrow sits between them. This breaks the rule that every raid line shows in one place. The timer is only about 28px, so it is not a 56px hero.
findings.fix: Keep one 20px f-cond pill, 'extract 152m', and drop the 'extraction c available' pill. Remove the arrow, or fold it into the pill. Raise the timer to 40-56px f-cond 800 in tx-1, with 8px between it and the pill.

findings.what: The saturated green slab (about 410x34px) with a 30px 'hp 100' is the loudest object on screen. It outweighs the ammo hero and the lime-selected slot. It is also butted against the screen corner with no margin. It uses a green outside the --ok token and fights the lime accent.
findings.fix: Make it 6-8px tall, with the 'hp 100' number at 20px beside it. Use --ok green, or --danger below 30%. Inset it 48px from the left and 32px from the bottom edge, and align it with the hotbar's left edge.

findings.where: left column (bots panel, 'pillager' bar, concealed badge, codex entry, controller connected, f1 controls)
findings.what: Six unrelated widgets are scattered down the left edge, each with its own fill, border and left offset (x≈8, 14, 12, 16). Text sizes of 13-16px are below the 16px floor. 'pillager' and the green bar sit as a loose box. This reads as clutter, not one system.
findings.fix: Put everything on one 16px left margin, with 8px vertical gaps, using the single --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Merge 'controller connected' into the 'keyboard' tag. Raise all minimum text to 16px. Drop the 'pillager' bar or merge it with the hp bar.

findings.what: The money list is a dense table: 14px names against right-aligned $ values, with a chevron and a bold header. The 'you' row is not distinguished. It reads as a debug list and draws the eye before the extraction state does.
findings.fix: Use 16px rows with 8px row padding and a 1px --ui-line divider. Mark the 'you' row with tx-1 and a 3px lime or amber left bar, and give the others tx-2. Put the header in label size, tx-2, without bold.

findings.where: world labels ('the long dock cache', 'sentry r-57', 'pillager · sentry · 19m', blue 'pillager' tag)
findings.what: The lilac text for the cache name is a colour outside the token set. The orange sentry labels sit on the orange floor and are hard to read, and the sentry label overlaps the character. The blue 'pillager' tag sits on top of the second character.
findings.fix: Draw all world labels at 16px tx-1 on a 70% --ui-void pill with 4px padding, and offset them 12px above their target. Use the rarity colour only as a 3px bar. Use --danger for hostile labels. Remove the lilac.

findings.what: Nine slots are always shown, and eight of them are dim ghost icons. This is heavy at the bottom edge. The ammo card is good, but its 'b / i backpack' and '3 items $1,220' lines are 14px. The slots have mixed border treatments: a lime frame on slot 1, a blue tint on slot 4, and a white-outlined slot 2.
findings.fix: Dim empty slots to about 40% with no icon. Use one border rule: lime 2px for the active slot only, with a rarity bar of 3px on the others. Raise the ammo card's secondary lines to 16px tx-2, and align the card's bottom edge with the hotbar (both at 32px from the bottom).

findings.what: The toast floats mid-screen at 16px above the hotbar in a fill that differs from the other panels, so it looks like a one-off. The 'f1 controls' chip sits at a random x and has a clear grey box with a key cap, unlike the other chips.
findings.fix: Move toasts to the left feed. Align 'f1 controls' to the controls line, mid-bottom left, as the owner specified. Give both the --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius.

findings.what: This panel is a different shape and fill from the top-left panel, and its chevron and 16px text are hard to read. The panel is clipped close to the edge (about 18px from the top and 20px from the right) and does not align with the left panel's inset (8px).
findings.fix: Use the same panel style and inset it 24px from the top and right. Match the left panel's 24px inset. Use a 3px lime or amber left bar only when a contract is active.

v.verdict: The screen is a different one from the earlier player 2 card: it is now a title menu with a strong lime main button and a gold wordmark. It is still weakened by a toast that overlaps the controls legend, a stray 'player 2 window' label, and large dead areas.

findings.where: bottom toast 'in pillager's party · ascend at the lift to join' over the controls legend
findings.what: The toast sits on top of the legend row (wasd, mouse, lmb, e, f1). It clips the key caps and half-hides the words 'move', 'aim', 'fire' and 'search'. Both lines become unreadable.
findings.fix: Move the toast to y≈940, at least 24px above the legend, or drop the legend on this screen. Give the toast a --ui-panel fill, a 1px --ui-line-hi border, 16px f-cond 600 text and 16px padding. Keep it from overlapping anything.

findings.what: A small grey label floats between the button and the saves list with no clear job. It reads as stray debug text and breaks the vertical rhythm.
findings.fix: Remove it, or turn it into a 16px tx-2 label inside a 56px header row that has a 1px --ui-line divider. If it must stay, put 24px of space above it and 32px below.

findings.what: The wordmark is a glossy amber gradient. The guide bans gradient washes, and amber is the warn/P1 colour. It also competes with the lime button, so two bold elements fight for first look.
findings.fix: Use a flat --tx-1 wordmark at 56px f-cond 800, or keep the gold only as a 3px underline bar. Keep the lime button as the single hot element.

findings.what: The rows have inconsistent heights (42 and 40px) and an 8px gap. The selected row has a thin lime outline and lime text. The name input and the buttons look the same, so nothing marks which is the input. The 'saves' label is at about 14px and dim.
findings.fix: Make every row 48px high with 8px gaps. Give the selected row a --ui-raised fill and a 3px lime left bar instead of a lime outline. Give the input a --ui-void fill with a visible caret. Set the 'saves' label at 16px tx-2.

findings.where: layout (content block in y 360-735, with 1080px of height)
findings.what: The content is a narrow stack in the middle. About 300px is empty above it and 250px below, with nothing anchoring the left and right sides. It reads as a template.
findings.fix: Add a 56px header and 72px footer with a 1px --ui-line divider. Put the legend and version in the footer on one baseline. Set the content block at 32px side margins and centre it on the optical centre (about y 480).

findings.where: top-right buttons 'go fullscreen' / 'settings' and top-centre 'keyboard' chip
findings.what: The buttons are at about 14px and sit 80px in from the right edge, not on the 5% margin. The teal 'keyboard' chip is an off-palette colour, since teal is reserved for extraction, and it is touching the top edge.
findings.fix: Align the buttons to the 5% margin (96px), at 16px f-cond 600 and 40px high. Recolour the chip with --ui-line-hi and --tx-2, and move it to y=24 or into the footer.

findings.where: version stamp 'v0.1171 · oct 27 10:37 pm et' and tagline
findings.what: The version stamp uses a slightly different style from the legend, with a different baseline and weight. The tagline 'ascend. pillage. extract.' is 18px tx-2 at low contrast.
findings.fix: Set the version at 14px f-body 500 on the same baseline as the legend. Raise the tagline to 20px, tx-2 (#aaa498), with +.04em tracking.

v.verdict: The card frame, header and footer follow the guide well, but the map is cluttered with overlapping labels and the contracts list is a flat column of same-weight rows with no focal point.

findings.where: map, the cache labels around the foreman office and the blast freezer, and 'cache' above the strongbox
findings.what: Labels stack and collide: 'cache' x4 at top right, 'cache cache cache cache' near the blast freezer, with leader lines crossing the text. The 'extract b' / 'stays open' / 'hot ground' / 'strongbox' cluster collides with the room outlines and each other. This reads as noise rather than information.
findings.fix: Collapse duplicate caches into a single icon with a count (e.g. 'cache x4'). Give every map label a 4px padded --ui-void plate at 80% opacity. Enforce a 12px minimum gap between labels and nudge colliding ones outward.

findings.where: map label type (cache, packing floor, the sump, scrap line, chill row)
findings.what: Many labels are ~14-15px in muted grey over a dark busy map, below the 16px minimum for anything read. Seen from a couch they are illegible. Label brightness is also inconsistent: some white, some grey, some teal, some red, with no clear logic.
findings.fix: Set all map labels to 16px f-cond 600 with +.04em tracking. Use only three tones: tx-1 for interactive or locked places, tx-2 for static areas, and semantic colour for extract (teal) and danger (red). Drop pure white.

findings.what: Eight identical rows with the same weight, title, price and progress repeating. There is no hierarchy: no row is selected or focused, and no hero number. The price '$320' and count '0/2' are small, right-aligned and stacked. Progress bars are thin grey lines that carry no information at 0%.
findings.fix: Put the contract name at 20px tx-1 and the reward at 20px --acc on the same line. Put the progress as a 4px bar with the count in 16px tx-2 beside it. Highlight the first or focused row with --ui-raised and a 3px lime left bar. Cut the header to '0/8' and drop 'done'.

findings.where: map, route and waypoint state / player marker
findings.what: The amber player arrow sits at the very bottom edge, partly clipped by the map border. Waypoint and player marker are small and easy to miss, and the map offers no focus or cursor state for the pad.
findings.fix: Add 24px of inner padding to the map bounds, or clamp markers so the arrow's 40px disc stays inside. Draw a 2px lime reticle for the cursor and a bright waypoint pin at 24px.

findings.what: The title is bold and good, but 'sector map' is a muted subtitle at nearly the same size, so there are two competing title-weight items. The right-hand '6pm · clear' is larger than the label tier and sits tight beside the X button, which is a 1px-bordered box of a different style from the rest.
findings.fix: Set 'sector map' to 16px tx-2 baseline-aligned with the title. Set the time to 16px tx-2 with 24px right margin before the X. Match the X button border to --ui-line-hi at 4px radius, 40x40.

findings.where: footer, 'click to set a waypoint' and 'surveyed 2%'
findings.what: Both are small (~15px) muted text on the left and read as a hint sentence, which the guide counts as clutter. 'surveyed 2%' is a status buried in the footer. The 'm close' keycap is yellow-filled and the lone lime accent on the screen, which is correct, but 'close' is tiny.
findings.fix: Drop the explanatory sentence in favour of a '[click] waypoint' keycap, in the same keycap style as 'm close'. Move 'surveyed 2%' to the map's top-left corner as a 16px label. Set 'close' to 16px tx-1.

findings.what: The map has a thick grey 8px double border that doesn't match the 1px --ui-line-hi panels around it. The map panel and contracts panel have different top and bottom insets (map starts at y=160 with a border, contracts at 160 with a fill). The result looks like two assembled widgets.
findings.fix: Use a 1px --ui-line-hi border at 4px radius on both panels. Align the top and bottom edges exactly and make the gap between them 24px (--sp-3).

findings.what: Lime is absent on the map and teal, red, amber, blue and white all compete. The red hatched zone and red encampment labels have close hues to the danger circle, and the blue block (water) adds a sixth colour with no legend.
findings.fix: Desaturate the blue water fill to ~15% opacity and keep red strictly for hostile. Mark the selected map target with --acc so lime keeps its meaning of 'selected'.

v.verdict: The minimap ping reads and the hud is mostly clean and lower case, but small type, a crowded left side, a blank minimap and a loose type scale keep it at a solid but not yet polished 3.

findings.what: The minimap is about 300x300 and nearly empty: a large dead black area, a thick white bar, and tiny ping glyphs (about 10px) crowded into the top edge. The solo ping, which is what this shot is about, is hard to pick out. The 'n' north marker is 11px and floats next to the pings. The chevron sits on top of the map.
findings.fix: Make ping markers at least 16px with a 2px dark outline and a short pulse ring. Move the north marker to a fixed corner tick. Crop or fill the empty area. Put the collapse chevron in the header row, not over the map.

findings.what: An 8-row leaderboard of about 14-15px text with tight 18px row pitch sits in the mid-left. Below the 16px minimum, it looks dense, and the lone purple name (fbi_surveillance_van) has no meaning. The $ values are fine, but it competes with gameplay and the codex toast below it.
findings.fix: Raise to 16px with a 24px row pitch. Show only you plus the 3 nearest ranks, or collapse by default. Drop the purple, or make it your one declared player tint. Give the panel a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 8px padding.

findings.where: hud type scale across the screen
findings.what: Sizes are scattered: 9:00 at about 28px, extract 141m at 16px, tiny hotbar numbers (about 11px), footer 'b / i backpack' and '4 items $1,560' at about 14px, a 56px ammo hero, and 'hp 100' at 32px in a flat green bar. Hotbar slot numbers and the 'f' tag are below the readable floor at 1080.
findings.fix: Snap to 56/32/20/16/14. Make slot numbers and ammo counts 16px. Set the timer to 32px. Set the footer to 16px --tx-2.

findings.where: bottom-left hp bar and 'f1 controls' chip
findings.what: The hp bar is a flat full-saturation green slab with tight text, and it sits at x=24 while the leaderboard sits at x=10 and the codex toast at x=16, so the left edges don't line up. The 'f1 controls' chip is small (about 14px) and floats at x=435, detached from the hotbar and the hp bar.
findings.fix: Put one 48px left margin on hp, the leaderboard and the toast. Use a 16px chip text size. Give the hp bar a dark track, a 4px radius and a 20px label.

findings.what: The selected slot (2) has a yellow border, but slot 4 has a blue fill and an 'f' tag, so two slots read as active. Empty slots are dim silhouettes at about 30% opacity, which is low contrast. Slot sizes are consistent, but the yellow border is thin and gold-ish, not the lime --acc.
findings.fix: Use a single 3px --acc border and a --ui-raised fill on the selected slot only. Move the 'f' quick-slot hint into the label size. Raise the empty silhouettes to about 45% opacity.

findings.what: A chevron-only collapsed row at 16px bold. It is not aligned with the minimap's inner edge and has a different border and fill from the leaderboard panel.
findings.fix: Use the same panel fill, 1px border and 4px radius as the leaderboard. Align to the minimap width and use 8px padding.

findings.what: The 9:00 has no panel and sits on a busy tile, so it competes with the grey scenery. The teal extract chip has a small arrow marker below it that floats alone.
findings.fix: Add a 0.6 alpha dark pill behind the timer. Attach the arrow to the chip as a 6px notch, or draw it as a screen-edge indicator.

v.verdict: The in-raid HUD is functional and mostly lower case, but it is crowded and uses small text and inconsistent panel styling, and the new sentry ping labels are tiny, low-contrast and sit on a busy tile.

findings.where: sentry ping label under the sentry ("you · sentry · 17m") and the "sentry r-46" tag
findings.what: The labels are about 12px orange text on a mid-tone ground with no plate. They fall below the 16px minimum, contrast is poor, and the "you · sentry · 17m" line collides with the crosshair ring and the gun art. The two labels are stacked with different styles (grey plate vs bare orange).
findings.fix: Put both on one --ui-panel plate at 85% opacity with 1px --ui-line-hi. Use 16px f-cond 600 in --tx-1. Show distance in --tx-2. Place it 16px above the sentry, clear of the ring. Show one label, not two.

findings.what: Eight rows of 14-15px text and values in a dense list. It is the largest panel on screen and competes with the clock for attention. Row heights are cramped (about 18px). The one purple row (fbi_surveillance_van) has no legend. The player's own row has no highlight. Under the quiet-HUD order this is clutter.
findings.fix: Collapse it by default to a single header line and open it on a key, or cut it to the top 3 plus you. Set rows to 16px with 24px height. Give the 'you' row a 3px --acc left bar and --tx-1 text. Drop the purple, or add a rarity glyph.

findings.what: The two feed lines use different bar colours (grey, amber) and different plate widths. They carry explaining sentences ("gold glow marks the box"), which is a defect. Text is about 15px. The feed sits directly on the f1 controls tag and the hp bar, so the bottom-left is crowded.
findings.fix: Shorten to "contract item nearby" and drop the explanation. Use one plate style: 16px text, 3px --warn bar for contracts, --ui-line-hi for info. Move the feed up 24px above the f1 tag. Make the plates the same width.

findings.where: hud bottom-right ammo card and hotbar
findings.what: The hero ammo number (30, about 56px) is correct, but the card packs five text levels (name, hero, /60, backpack hint, item count and value) at 14-16px in a fixed box. The hotbar slots 3 and 5-0 are a flat dark grey with weak silhouettes. The empty slots read as clutter, and the selected slot's lime outline is thin.
findings.fix: Drop the 'b / i backpack' line and the item count into a single 16px --tx-2 line. Dim empty slots to 40% opacity. Make the selected slot's border 3px --acc with --ui-raised fill. Keep the 8px gaps.

findings.what: The 'hp 100' label is a tall condensed 30px in white on a green fill. It is the loudest text in the corner, bigger than the title scale. The bar has no frame and a 6px offset from the screen edge, which differs from the other panels' 16px margin.
findings.fix: Use 20px f-cond 700 on a 12px-high bar with a 1px --ui-line-hi frame and --ok fill. Put the number inside the bar's right edge, or inline at 20px. Set the left margin to 24px to match the panels.

findings.what: The minimap's cyan and amber markers are about 8px and hard to tell apart. The panel has a black fill with no border, unlike the scoreboard, which has a 1px border. The contracts bar is a different width from the map and carries a lone chevron.
findings.fix: Give the minimap and contracts a shared --ui-panel fill and 1px --ui-line-hi border, with a 4px radius on both. Enlarge the markers to 12px. Align the contracts bar flush to the map width.

findings.what: The clock is about 28px white text with no plate. It floats on a brown ground with weak contrast. The teal extract pill reads '14lm' because of the glyph spacing, which is probably an 'm' with tight kerning. The pointer tick below it is tiny.
findings.fix: Put the clock on a --ui-panel plate and use 32px f-cond 700. Fix the tracking on the distance label to +.04em. Set the pill height to 32px and the pointer to 12px.

findings.what: It is a small 16px tag crammed against the hotbar edge and the feed. It has a different fill and corner from the other plates, and its 'f1' keycap is nearly the same tone as the plate, so it is hard to read.
findings.fix: Use the standard plate (--ui-panel, 1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius). Give the keycap an --ui-raised fill with a --tx-1 glyph. Keep a 16px gap from the hotbar and the feed.

v.verdict: A mostly clean, consistent in-raid HUD with a strong ammo hero number and a good quiet hotbar, but the top-left roster panel is a wall of small text and dead rows, the hp bar is the odd one out, and the 'wallet' this shot is named for (0 items $0) is a tiny afterthought.

findings.what: A large panel (about 360x190) of 13px dim text lists seven dead bots plus 'you -'. The '- dead' column repeats seven times and nothing in it can be acted on. It is the biggest block on the screen, and it is clutter that pulls the eye away from the play area. The title is white and bold while the rows are dim grey, and the pink fbi_surveillance_van row is an unexplained colour. Text is below the 16px label floor.
findings.fix: Collapse it to the one-line summary '0 out · 7 dead' (folded by default, chevron to expand). If it stays open, drop dead rows to 40% opacity, delete the repeated '- dead' column, use 16px/600 rows on a 24px pitch, and recolour fbi_surveillance_van to tx-1 unless the colour has a meaning.

findings.where: bottom-right ammo card, wallet line 'b / i backpack  0 items $0'
findings.what: The two wallet values are 14px, tx-2 text crammed on one baseline at the card's bottom edge with about 8px padding. 'backpack' and '0 items $0' are the lowest-contrast, smallest text in the card. For a shot meant to show the wallet this is the weakest element, and the gap between the 56px hero '30 / 60' and this line is too big.
findings.fix: Raise to 16px/600 f-cond in tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better. Give the card 16px padding and a 1px --ui-line divider above the line. Colour the '$0' tx-1 and keep '0 items' in tx-2 so the money reads first. Drop the 'b / i' key hint into a small key chip like the F1 one.

findings.where: bottom-left hp bar vs the rest of the HUD
findings.what: The bar is a flat green slab with 'hp 100' at about 32px in a different bold weight, with no panel, no border and a different radius from the hotbar and ammo card. It is the only element not on a --ui-panel card, and a full-green bar says nothing in the state that matters. The green is also close to the map's green and loses contrast against grass.
findings.fix: Put the bar in a 4px-radius --ui-panel card with a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Use a 24px high fill with --ok, and print 'hp 100' at 20px/600 inside it or left of it, not 32px bold. Turn the fill --warn below 50% and --danger below 25%.

findings.what: Eight slots hold dim ghost weapon silhouettes at about 25% contrast, which reads as an empty grid. The slot number is 12px and the weapon icons are tiny relative to the slots. Only slot 2 is active, and its lime border is the right focus cue, but the gap between the active slot and the others is extreme.
findings.fix: Hide the silhouettes for slots the player does not own (show just the number, at 14px tx-2). Raise the slot numbers to 16px. Keep the lime 2px border on the active slot only.

findings.where: top-centre timer and extract chip '9:00 / extract 14m'
findings.what: The 9:00 timer is white at about 28px with no backing and sits on busy terrain, so contrast varies with the map. The teal 'extract 14m' chip underneath is a good use of the extract colour. The arrow below it is a stray glyph with no label.
findings.fix: Put the timer on the same 80% scrim chip as the extract line, or add a 2px dark text shadow. Align the chip width to the timer, and attach the arrow to the chip's bottom edge with a 4px gap.

findings.what: The minimap is mostly black void with a white bar graphic through the middle, so its legibility is low, and the chevron buttons on both panels differ in size from the roster chevron. 'contracts 0/8' is a good small header, but its panel has a bevel that the roster panel lacks.
findings.fix: Fill empty minimap areas with --ui-bg at 60% and dim the white bar. Make every collapse chevron 16px in the same stroke. Use one border style (1px --ui-line-hi, 4px radius) on the roster, minimap and contracts panels.

findings.where: 'f1 controls' chip, bottom-left of the hotbar
findings.what: A 14px chip floats about 110px left of the hotbar with a gap that has no alignment to the hotbar or hp bar. It is a very low-priority hint, but it is easy to read as a stray label.
findings.fix: Left-align it to the hotbar's left edge, 8px above the hotbar's top edge, at 16px tx-2.

v.verdict: This is a raid HUD, not the player 2 title screen the earlier advice covered. The ammo block, hotbar and extract banner read cleanly, but the bots list is crowded and low-contrast, the hp bar clashes with every other panel, and one capital letter is on screen.

findings.where: left feed toast 'contract Item nearby · gold glow marks the box'
findings.what: The capital 'I' in 'Item' breaks the all-lower-case rule. The line is also an explaining sentence ('gold glow marks the box'), and the amber text and bar sit on a busy green map with no solid panel fill.
findings.fix: Render it as 'contract item nearby' and drop the 'gold glow marks the box' clause. Use a 16px f-cond 600 tx-1 label on a --ui-panel fill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 8px padding. Keep the 3px warn bar on the left.

findings.what: A flat bright green fill with a large 'hp 100' label in tx-1 on top of it has weak contrast. The bar is the loudest element in the HUD and competes with the ammo hero number. It shares no border, radius or panel language with the hotbar or ammo block.
findings.fix: Put it in a --ui-panel track with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius, 16px high, with an --ok fill. Set 'hp' at 16px tx-2 and '100' at 20px tx-1 outside the fill, left of the bar. Align its bottom edge with the hotbar bottom at y 1062.

findings.what: Eight rows at about 14px, with tx-2 names and '- dead' on every row, put a wall of grey text over a busy map. Name and status are low contrast. The 'dead' repetition is clutter. The 'fbi_surveillance_van' purple name is a stray colour.
findings.fix: Collapse dead rows to a single footer line, '0 out · 7 dead', which already exists. Show only living entries at 16px, with names in tx-1 and values in tx-2 at 4.5:1 or better. Use a --ui-panel fill at .92 alpha. Keep the purple only if it means a rarity or player colour.

findings.what: It is about 16px, sits tight against the hotbar's top-left corner (about 12px gap) and floats with no panel language. It is easy to miss, and a font that looks like 'fl' reads ambiguously.
findings.fix: Give it a 24px gap above the hotbar at y≈925. Use a --ui-panel pill with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and a keycap-style 'f1' in tx-1, with 'controls' at 16px tx-2.

findings.what: Seven dim empty weapon silhouettes at near-equal weight make the bar heavy and noisy. The selected slot 2 has a gold outline, which is the wrong accent: --acc lime is reserved for selected.
findings.fix: Dim empty slots to 40% and drop their silhouettes to a plain number only. Switch the selected outline to a 2px --acc border with a --ui-raised fill. Use 8px gaps, 56px slots and 16px slot numbers.

findings.what: The minimap has tiny, near-illegible glyphs at the top edge and a hard-clipped white stripe pattern. The contracts bar uses a different border and fill than the bots panel. The chevrons are tiny.
findings.fix: Use a 1px --ui-line-hi border and --ui-panel on both, with matching 4px radii and 8px padding. Make the glyphs at least 12px. Set the 'contracts' label at 16px f-cond 600 and 0/8 in tx-1.

findings.what: A small chip with a green outline and a bold green label is another one-off style. It is about 14px and lime-ish, so it competes with the accent.
findings.fix: Restyle it as a 16px tx-2 label on --ui-panel with a 1px --ui-line border, or remove it after the first 3 seconds.

findings.what: The 56px hero '30 / 60' works, but the footer row 'b / i backpack' and '6 items $1,020' sits at about 14px in tx-2 on a dark panel, near the floor. The '60' reserve shares the hero's weight.
findings.fix: Raise the footer to 16px with a tx-2 that clears 4.5:1. Set '/ 60' at 32px tx-2 so '30' is the single hero. Keep the 8px grid padding of 16px.

v.verdict: The raid HUD is much quieter than before: one banner, no left-column clutter, and a clean hotbar with a clear ammo card. The unmodified screen is now dominated by a large 'want easy mode?' modal whose title is weak, whose countdown has no label, and whose buttons don't match the rest of the UI.

findings.what: The title is only about 32px with a faint lime tab at the top-left. The '10' countdown floats at the top-right with no label or ring, so it reads as a stray number. The 'y yes' / 'n no' buttons are 100px tall and about 405px wide, which is much larger than any other button in the game. There is a lot of dead space, and the modal has no close x or other card chrome.
findings.fix: Cut the card to about 640x300. Set the title to 32px f-cond 700 tx-1. Replace '10' with a thin 3px lime countdown bar along the card's bottom edge. Make the buttons 64px tall, 20px f-cond 600, with a 4px radius and 16px between them. Put the key hint in a 16px label, 'y' left of 'yes', not as a prefix glyph.

findings.where: modal scrim and world behind it
findings.what: There is no scrim, so the full-brightness map competes with the modal. The player can still see the sprite and the HUD, and the bright orange and green ground makes the dark card feel pasted on. The card's dark fill does not separate cleanly from the dark buildings behind it at the edges.
findings.fix: Apply a --scrim rgba(6,7,8,.80) layer behind the modal. Add a 1px --ui-line-hi border to the card, with a 4px radius.

findings.what: The hp bar is a 32px fill with a 'hp 100' label in about 32px f-cond. It is bolder than the ammo hero number, so two heroes compete. It is only 24px from the left edge and sits flush against the bottom edge with no margin. The armour bar is blue and uses a different font weight and size from hp. Both bars are about 400px wide and heavy.
findings.fix: Make both bars 8px tall. Put 'hp 100' and 'armour 60' labels at 16px f-cond 600 above the bars, tx-2 for armour. Make hp --ok green, and --danger below 30%. Inset the group 48px from the left and 32px from the bottom. Align its left edge with the panel's left margin, and make its width match the hotbar's slot 1-4 span.

findings.where: top-centre score card, extract pill, minimap and goals chip
findings.what: The 'team score' card is cramped. '0 sp', 'you 0 sp' and 'p2 0 sp' are three sizes in 11-16px type, and the '9:58' timer is small and tucked under them. The card is flush with the top edge, with no margin. The extract pill butts directly against the card's bottom edge with 0px gap, and the teal arrow beneath it floats over a crate. The minimap's collapse chevron and the goals chip use two different border radii and fills.
findings.fix: Give the score card 16px padding and a 16px top margin. Set the timer to 32px f-cond 800 tx-1. Set the sp lines to 16px, and put 'you' and 'p2' in P1 amber and P2 cyan. Leave 8px between the card and the extract pill. Use one 4px radius and --ui-panel fill on the minimap, goals chip and cards.

findings.what: The hotbar is solid, but the nine unselected slots are very dark, so the grey weapon silhouettes have low contrast (about 2:1). The slot numbers are only about 14px and in muted grey. The selected slot gets only a thin amber border, while slot 6 has a blue tint, so it is unclear which one is active. The 'f' key tag on slot 6 is tiny.
findings.fix: Raise the silhouettes to tx-2 at 60% opacity (4.5:1 or better). Make slot numbers 16px. Mark the active slot with a 2px --acc border plus --ui-raised fill, and tint no other slot. Make the 'f' tag 16px in a 20px chip.

findings.what: The ammo card is the best element on screen, with a 56px hero number, but 'support mg' is right-aligned at about 28px, so it competes with the number. The '/ 360' reserve is nearly as heavy as the '60'. The card is only about 8px from the screen's right edge and does not match the hotbar's bottom alignment. It touches the screen margin where the hp bar uses a 24px margin.
findings.fix: Set 'support mg' to 16px f-cond 600 tx-2, left-aligned. Set '/ 360' to 20px tx-2. Align the card's bottom edge with the hotbar's bottom edge. Give it a 48px right margin, to mirror the hp bar's 48px left margin.

findings.what: The chip is tiny, about 14px, on a dark box that sits just above the armour bar. It is cramped there and has a different fill from the other panels. It does not follow the owner's order to sit mid-bottom left, because it is crowded by the armour bar and stands about 20px from the hotbar.
findings.fix: Make it a 16px label chip with 8px padding and a 4px radius on --ui-panel. Move it 16px above the hp group's top edge, left-aligned with it. Give the 'f1' key a 20px --ui-raised keycap.

findings.what: The minimap is mostly black with sparse markers and a large empty lower half, so its small icons are hard to read. Its markers (n, arrows and diamonds) are 10px or smaller, and the white road strips at the right are visually louder than the player arrow.
findings.fix: Crop the map to the explored area and draw markers at 16px minimum. Drop the road strips to --ui-line. Make the player arrow the single --acc marker. Add an 8px gap between the minimap and the goals chip.

v.verdict: the left feed and bots list are gone and the hud is quieter, but the easy-mode modal sits on a live raid with a flat, unpolished card and the hp, armour and hotbar details are still loose.

findings.what: The card has no border and no scrim, so it floats over a bright map. The title sits at 32px but the card is mostly empty. The '10' countdown is a small grey number in the top right with no label. The 'yes' button is a full lime slab, so it is louder than the title. 'n no' is a thin outline with a low-contrast border. The lime tab at the top-left corner looks like a stray artifact.
findings.fix: Add a --scrim at .80 behind the card. Give the card a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Shrink the card to about 640x300. Make the countdown a 56px --fs-hero number in --acc, or a thin lime progress bar along the card top. Keep 'yes' as the single lime button. Give 'no' a 2px --ui-line-hi border with tx-1 text. Drop the stray lime tab or turn it into the countdown bar.

findings.where: hp bar and armour bar, bottom-left (x 24-430, y 968-1070)
findings.what: The hp bar is a flat green slab with a 36px 'hp 100' that is larger than any other HUD text, and it nearly touches the screen bottom. The armour bar is a saturated blue pill with a different height and radius. Neither has a track or border, the bottoms don't align with the hotbar, and the two bars fight each other for attention.
findings.fix: Use matching 16px-high bars with a --ui-panel track, a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius. Colour them --ok for hp and a muted --r-rare for armour. Set the labels in 16px f-cond 600 tx-2 and the values in 20px tx-1, outside the fill. Pull both bars up so the hp bar bottom is at y 1062, the same as the hotbar. Leave 8px between the bars.

findings.what: The empty slots show full-size dim gun silhouettes that look like owned items, and the numbers are small. The selected slot has a thin amber border that reads as a player colour, not the lime 'selected' signal. The green and purple slot fills compete with the selected state. The 'f' badge on slot 5 is tiny at about 10px.
findings.fix: Dim empty slots to 40% and show only the number. Make the selected slot a 2px --acc border on a --ui-raised fill. Show rarity as a 3px bar at the slot bottom instead of a fill. Raise slot numbers to 16px. Make the 'f' badge 16px.

findings.where: top-left 'keyboard' chip (x 0-105, y 6-32) and 'f1 controls' hint (x 412-537, y 924-952)
findings.what: The chip is jammed against the screen corner with no margin, in bold green text that clashes with the palette. The 'f1 controls' hint sits right on the hotbar edge with a flat dark fill, about 14px text and no keycap.
findings.fix: Move the chip to x 48, y 24 as a --ui-panel pill with 16px tx-2 text and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Move the f1 hint up to y≈915, which leaves a 24px gap above the hotbar. Draw 'f1' as a keycap in tx-1 and 'controls' at 16px tx-2.

findings.what: The panel is glued to the top edge with no top margin and a flat fill. 'you 0 sp' and 'p2 0 sp' are about 14px and low-contrast, and neither is tinted amber or cyan. The '0 sp' hero at about 40px does not match the 56px hero spec. The teal extract chip overlaps the panel's bottom edge.
findings.fix: Set a 16px top margin and a 1px --ui-line-hi border. Make the hero 56px. Set the 'you' value in amber and the 'p2' value in cyan, both at 16px tx-1. Put the extract chip 8px below the panel instead of overlapping it.

findings.what: The weapon name is small grey text above a huge '30 / 180', so the ammo hero is about 80px, well over the 56px spec. The panel hugs the right edge with 8px of margin and does not align with the hotbar bottom.
findings.fix: Set the ammo hero to 56px, the weapon name to 20px tx-1, and '/ 180' to 20px tx-2. Set a 48px right margin and align the panel bottom to y 1062.

findings.what: The minimap is a plain dark box with tiny glyphs and a clipped white strip. 'goals 0/3' is a different panel style from the rest of the HUD, with a different border and a chevron.
findings.fix: Put the minimap in a --ui-panel frame with a 1px --ui-line-hi border and 4px radius at a 48px margin. Match the goals row to the same border and radius, with 16px labels.

v.verdict: The hub's one-hot-label hierarchy is clear, with 'enter raid!' as the lime hero. The top-right currency strip floats unframed on the void, the lower-case stat text is tiny, and the exclamation mark and the '***experimental feature may glitch***' caption read as template and debug text.

findings.where: top-right currency strip: '$4,471,337  98,761 xp  stash $0 bag $0'
findings.what: The strip has no panel and sits half over the dark letterbox and half over the wall. The stash/bag text is dim grey on near-black and about 14px. The three groups have uneven gaps, and 'xp' is a different size from the number. Hero-size numbers compete with the lime title. It breaks the career HUD order of a vertical 1 by 1 list of equal-size items.
findings.fix: Put the money and xp in a --ui-panel card (4px radius, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 16px padding) inset 48px from the right and 32px from the top. Stack the rows vertically, each 20px f-cond 600 tx-1 with a 16px tx-2 label. Move 'stash $0 bag $0' into this stack at tx-2 and 16px. Cut the 56px money figure to 32px so it doesn't compete with 'enter raid'.

findings.where: station labels (the gambler, mainframe, shop, settings, the stash, fashion, last pour)
findings.what: Each label is a separate black chip with a different width, and the baselines are inconsistent: some sit above the pad and some sit on the wall. The 6 labels have no focus or selected state. 'the stash' and 'fashion' overlap character sprites and glow circles. The 'shop, craft, and hire' comma list reads as a sentence.
findings.fix: Use one label style: --ui-panel fill, 1px --ui-line-hi border, 4px radius, 8px by 16px padding, 20px f-cond 600 tx-1. Anchor each label 16px above its pad. Show the nearest station's label with a 2px --acc border and leave the others at 70% opacity. Shorten 'shop, craft, and hire' to 'shop'.

findings.where: '***experimental feature may glitch***' above the last pour
findings.what: This is amber debug-style text with asterisks, about 14px, in a long chip wider than every other label. It reads as a placeholder and it breaks the straight-copy rule. It's also an explaining sentence on screen.
findings.fix: Remove the asterisks and the sentence. Show a 16px f-cond 600 --warn 'beta' tag, 8px by 8px padding, in the label's top-right corner.

findings.what: The lime text sits on a black chip at about 56px with a tight 8px pad, and it overlaps a wall pillar and the teal pad ring beneath. The exclamation mark is the arcade wink the guide forbids. It uses the hero size on a label, not a button. A Fortnite-style CTA would be a filled lime button with --acc-ink text.
